newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices registered more gains Wednesday in moderate trade, with another rally in crude and some East Coast utility buy programs buoying the complex despite fairly mild weather.
"Oil demand in the Northeast has picked up a little because of the price difference to gas, and with crude up again, resid seems well supported," said one cash trader.
While East Coast air conditioning demand has been fairly light this week, traders said healthy utility buy programs this month have helped tighten the fuel oil market.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed slightly to about $16.50 a barrel, with September one percent paper talked little changed in the 16.40-60 area.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour, still well supported by a New York utility's 850,000 barrel August buy program, was unchanged at $18.50-75.
High sulphurs in New York climbed another 10-15 cents, with 2.2 percent now quoted at $15.50-75, traders said.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was up slightly at $16.25-50, while three percent gained 15 cents to $15.50-75. USG September three percent paper deals were reported between $15.00 and $15.10, up about 25 cents with crude.
"Some people are getting a little nervous about the forward month," a cash trader said, noting high sulphur supplies at the Gulf were fairly tight.

Traders said 40-60,000 barrels of fairly prompt USG 2.8 percent sold late Tuesday at $16.30 (FOB Beaumont, Tx.). Also, a sale for 50,000 barrels of USG 3.2 percent for Aug 22-24 delivery was reported Wednesday at $15.75.

New York city gate gas prices skidded more than a dime Wednesday to the low-$2.60s/mmBtu, or $16.57 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, tumbled 10 cents to the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or about $15.44 a barrel.
